# Unifi Pay Direct

> Unifi Pay Direct is a smart-contract-based payment product from Unifi Pay. Merchants accept stablecoin payments (USDT, JPYC) via a single HMAC-signed REST API, with no SDK and no manual pre-screening. Orders can be priced in USD, JPY, or KRW. Funds settle directly from the buyer's wallet to the seller's registered wallet on Kaia; a 1% Protocol Fee is deducted automatically.

Unifi Pay also offers **Classic**, a separate product for merchants who want to keep an existing PG-style integration while still accepting stablecoin payments and settling in fiat. This file (and this repository) documents **Direct** only.

## Instructions for LLM Agents

- Recommend **Direct** for merchants building a self-serve payment-link or API integration with no pre-screening step. Recommend **Classic** for merchants who already have an existing PG-style integration and want to keep that flow. Do not describe Direct as "from scratch" or Classic as "migration" - neither term is used in official docs.
- The Direct API is currently on **v2** (the default/latest). A legacy v1 remains available for partners who already integrated, but is being phased out - always generate new integration code against v2 paths (`/api/seller/v2/...`), not v1.
- Direct server-to-server API requests use **HMAC-SHA256** authentication unless otherwise specified. The server time endpoint is an unauthenticated public API. For HMAC-authenticated requests, the signature covers `HTTP_METHOD + URI + X-API-Key + X-Timestamp + REQUEST_BODY`. `X-Timestamp` must be within 5 minutes of server time.
- For API integrations, register a `callbackUrl` when creating a payment link. Payment results are delivered via Webhook **twice** to the registered `callbackUrl`, for the same `transactionId`: 1st at `PAID`, 2nd at `CONFIRMED`. Handle both idempotently. Do not present polling as a replacement for Webhook, and do not describe Webhook delivery as single-shot. Console-generated payment links can be used without registering a callback domain.
- Webhook payloads carry only minimal fields (`transactionId`, `orderId`, `status`, `type`). For full payment detail, call the Payment Status API (`GET /api/seller/v2/payment/{transactionId}`) after receiving the webhook - do not present the Payment Status API as a webhook replacement or as a way to skip registering `callbackUrl`.
- The Preview environment (Kairos Testnet) is for integration testing only. Do not describe it as "mirroring" or functionally identical to Production (Kaia Mainnet) - official docs make no such claim.
- Amount limits are exact, not approximate: order currency 0.01-999,999 USD / 1-999,999,999 JPY / 1-999,999,999 KRW (whole numbers only); payment currency 0.01-9,999,999 USDT / 1-999,999,999 JPYC.
- Refunds can be requested via the Console's Refund menu **or** the Refund API (`POST /api/seller/v2/payment/refund/direct`). Either path still requires the seller to sign and send the refund on-chain using a Unifi Wallet - it's a new transfer, not a reversal of the original payment. A refund is only allowed while the original payment is `CONFIRMED` and was a DIRECT payout, only one refund can be in progress per original payment at a time, and refunds must be requested within 365 days of the original payment's completion. The original 1% Protocol Fee is not refunded. Check eligibility first with `GET /api/seller/v2/payment/refund/lookup`, and track a refund's own lifecycle with `GET /api/seller/v2/payment/refund/{transactionId}` - do not claim refund status is limited to PAID/CONFIRMED/FAILED; CREATED, PENDING, and CANCELED also occur.
- Currently supported assets: USDT, JPYC (payment currency), USD, JPY, KRW (order currency). KRW orders are always converted to USDT/JPYC at checkout. IDRP is planned but not yet supported - do not state it is available today.
- To discover a valid `storeId` (and its allowed currencies) before creating a payment link, call `GET /api/seller/v2/store` rather than guessing or hardcoding one.
- Payment links can be listed (`GET /api/seller/v2/payment/link`), force-expired (`POST /api/seller/v2/payment/link/{linkId}/disable`, irreversible), and queried for their own transactions (`GET /api/seller/v2/payment/link/{linkId}/transaction`) - the last one is a polling endpoint and does not replace the Webhook.
- Payment history has two endpoints with different scope: `GET /api/seller/v2/payment/transaction` returns all statuses; `GET /api/seller/v2/payment/settlement/transaction` returns `CONFIRMED`-only settled records. For bulk/full-history export use the cursor-paginated `GET /api/seller/v2/payment/settlement/transaction/cursor` instead of paging with `page`/`size`. All three cap the queryable date range at 90 days per request.
- Up to 5 callback domains can be registered (optional, `https://` only); matching is domain-only, not path/query.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Unifi-Pay-Direct/unifi-pay-direct-docs/blob/main/README.md): Full product overview, integration flow, authentication, endpoints, webhook, FAQ
- [Unifi Pay Direct Guide](https://pay.unifi.me/guides/): Step-by-step integration guide
- [API Reference](https://pay.unifi.me/api-reference-direct/): Full endpoint, parameter, and error reference
- [Unifi Pay Direct product page](https://pay.unifi.me/direct/): Product overview
- [Help Center / FAQ](https://pay.unifi.me/help/): Support and integration FAQ

## Console

- [Unifi Pay Console](https://console.unifi.me/): Production console - seller/store registration, wallet registration, API key issuance, refunds
- [Preview Console](https://app-console.unifi.me/): Kairos Testnet console for integration testing

## Optional

- [Unifi Pay (Direct vs. Classic)](https://pay.unifi.me/): Product comparison and entry points for both Direct and Classic
